name: AdminWatch Central
author: webstudiowadev

sections.description:
AdminWatch Central provides lightweight administration visibility. It lists users in roles capable of making material content or administrative changes, records each user’s latest successful login and latest observed password-change date after installation, displays a local password-strength estimate when a password is changed, shows MFA status for supported authentication providers, shows current active WordPress session counts, links to WordPress Site Health, and aggregates genuine front-end 404 URL paths.

404 request totals are maintained as small daily aggregates, so the Dashboard’s today and seven-day totals remain accurate without retaining individual requests.

Login and password-change metadata is recorded only after AdminWatch Central observes the relevant event. MFA status is available only for supported authentication providers and may show “Not detected” when status cannot be reliably determined. Active Session counts are read from current WordPress core session state for eligible users and are not stored by AdminWatch Central.

AdminWatch Central does not create or store its own copies of passwords or password hashes. It also does not store password history, login IP addresses, login history, session tokens, session metadata, MFA secrets, referrers, telemetry, external APIs, alerts or redirect tools.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the adminwatch-central folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install it through WordPress.
  2. Activate AdminWatch Central through the Plugins screen.
  3. Open AdminWatch Central from the administrator menu.
sections.faq:
Why does a user say “Not recorded yet”?

AdminWatch Central only records successful logins after it is installed. It does not guess historic login activity.

Does deactivation delete data?

No. Data is retained on deactivation. The optional delete-on-uninstall setting controls deletion when the plugin is removed.

Does AdminWatch Central send data to Web Studio WA?

No. AdminWatch Central works locally within WordPress and does not send telemetry to Web Studio WA.
